name: google-workspace
description: Google Workspace (Gmail, Calendar, Drive, Docs, Sheets, Slides, Forms, Tasks, Chat, Contacts, Apps Script) through the workspace-mcp stdio server at its core tool tier, on the operator's own OAuth grant; reads free, every write ungated and named
hits: Google Workspace (Gmail, Calendar, Drive, Docs, Sheets, Tasks, Apps Script)
surface: registration only (`toolbelt register google-workspace`) — `uvx workspace-mcp==1.25.0 --tool-tier core` runs locally (pinned: verbs[] is a classification of exactly that release) on the operator's OAuth grant and its 45 core tools appear in-session as mcp__google-workspace__<tool>; 25 reads, 20 ungated writes (send_gmail_message, manage_event, modify_sheet_values, update_script_content, …) with no belt code to gate them; the contract is the gate

origin.note: hello-gmail was a setup/debug scaffold (one CLAUDE.md, an untracked plan.md); its durable facts live in this CLAUDE.md. The server it configures is https://github.com/taylorwilsdon/google_workspace_mcp (PyPI `workspace-mcp`, 1.25.0 at vendoring), run from PyPI by uvx — no server code is vendored. The label taxonomy and triage routine carried into CLAUDE.md come from ~/Projects/gmail (github.com/RobGruhl/gmail-cleanup)

env.name: GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID
env.description: OAuth client id of the operator's own Desktop-app client in their Google Cloud project (APIs & Services > Credentials). Not a secret by itself, but it is paired with the secret below and lives beside it in the Keychain item

env.name: GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET
env.description: OAuth client secret of that Desktop-app client. Canonical home: macOS Keychain generic-password item service `google-workspace-oauth`; load it into the shell that launches the MCP client with: export GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET="$(security find-generic-password -s google-workspace-oauth -w)". Never in ~/.claude.json, ~/.codex/config.toml, or a shell rc file

env.name: OAUTHLIB_INSECURE_TRANSPORT
env.description: Lets oauthlib accept the server's http://localhost:8000 OAuth callback (loopback only — it is not a remote endpoint). workspace-mcp refuses the first-run consent flow without it

env.name: WORKSPACE_MCP_DISABLED_TOOLS
env.description: Comma-separated tool names the server refuses to register regardless of tier — the only narrowing knob the belt can apply to a hosted server's writes. Unset by default; see CLAUDE.md "Narrowing"

auth.flow: Google OAuth 2.0 authorization-code flow on the operator's own Desktop-app client: the server opens a browser consent page on first use (or when scopes change), Google redirects to http://localhost:8000/oauth2callback, and the access + refresh tokens are cached per account under ~/.google_workspace_mcp/credentials/. Every API call runs as the operator; the belt holds no credential
auth.login: Call any mcp__google-workspace__* read in-session (e.g. list_calendars) — a browser consent page opens; tick EVERY scope checkbox or the grant fails with "Scope has changed"
auth.identity: ls ~/.google_workspace_mcp/credentials/   (one <account>.json per granted account; never cat it — it holds the refresh token and the client secret)

caches.refresh: automatic refresh-token grant with no human; a revoked grant re-opens the browser consent on the next call
caches.revoke: rm ~/.google_workspace_mcp/credentials/<account>.json, then https://myaccount.google.com/permissions > remove the app
caches.note: workspace-mcp writes <account>.json mode 644; it carries refresh_token AND client_secret. chmod 600 it (the doctor's token-cache check warns until you do). GOOGLE_MCP_CREDENTIALS_DIR relocates the dir

caches.refresh: security add-generic-password -U -s google-workspace-oauth -a "$GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID" -w   (prompts for the secret; never pass it on argv)
caches.revoke: security delete-generic-password -s google-workspace-oauth; then delete the OAuth client in the Cloud console
caches.note: the long-lived client secret; the account field holds the client id so one item carries the pair

auth.note: OAuth scopes are requested by the server at the core tier (gmail.modify, gmail.send, calendar, drive, docs, spreadsheets, tasks, chat, contacts, script). `--read-only` or `--permissions gmail:drafts …` on the registration narrows the grant itself; the belt keeps the operator's current full core grant and narrows by contract instead (CLAUDE.md)

safeguards: No local gate is claimed: the belt ships no code on the call path, so it cannot enforce one. The server runs on the operator's own OAuth grant and can do exactly what the operator can do in Google's UI (SENSIBILITIES #13); the belt's contribution is the registration, the verb tiers, the permission profile derived from them, and the contract in CLAUDE.md (SENSIBILITIES #2).

Every core-tier write is tiered `write` with a note, so repo-integrity names all 20 on every doctor run; none is silently green. Three irreversible ones — update_script_content (full replace), manage_event delete, manage_task delete — are called out in the contract as human-in-UI actions.

Secrets never enter a config file: the registration carries ${GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID} / ${GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET} references that the MCP client expands from the process environment, and the secret's canonical home is the macOS Keychain (checks/smoke.mjs fails the smoke test if a literal ever lands in the registration block) (SENSIBILITIES #6, #11).

The token cache is the vendor's (~/.google_workspace_mcp/credentials/); checks/token-cache.mjs reports presence, mode and recorded expiry only — never a value — and warns while the file is group/world readable.
Narrowing is available at the registration, not claimed by default: WORKSPACE_MCP_DISABLED_TOOLS or `--read-only` remove write tools from the server before they reach a session.

verbs.name: search_gmail_messages
verbs.note: Gmail search syntax; the triage query is in CLAUDE.md; page_size ≤ 50 per call

verbs.name: get_gmail_messages_content_batch
verbs.note: ≤ 25 ids per call; two batches in parallel trip Google's per-user concurrency limit — serialize

verbs.name: get_drive_shareable_link
verbs.note: reads webViewLink and the current permission list; creates no permission (drive_tools.py, 1.25.0)

verbs.name: list_calendars
verbs.note: the cheapest live read — the doctor's identity probe

verbs.name: read_sheet_values
verbs.note: fails "Unable to parse range" when the tab does not exist — a missing tab, not an empty one

verbs.name: get_messages
verbs.note: Google Chat

verbs.name: search_messages
verbs.note: Google Chat

verbs.name: search_custom
verbs.note: Programmable Search; needs the operator's own search-engine id

verbs.name: generate_trigger_code
verbs.note: local code generation; calls no Google API

verbs.name: send_gmail_message
verbs.note: sends mail as the operator with no belt gate (no code here to gate in) and no undo; the contract is the gate — compose, show the human the full message and recipients, get an explicit yes for that payload, send once. Default to drafting (the extended tier's draft_gmail_message, or the claude.ai Gmail connector's create_draft) unless the human says send

verbs.name: manage_event
verbs.note: create/update/delete/rsvp on the operator's calendars, ungated; `delete` is irreversible and invitees are notified — a human does deletes in Google Calendar. Preview the event, get the yes, run once, re-read with get_events

verbs.name: manage_task
verbs.note: create/update/delete Google Tasks, ungated; delete is irreversible — human-in-UI

verbs.name: manage_contact
verbs.note: create/update/delete People contacts, ungated; reversible only via Google Contacts' 30-day undo

verbs.name: modify_sheet_values
verbs.note: overwrites the named range in place, ungated; Sheets version history is the undo. Always read_sheet_values the range first and show the diff; the cleanup pipeline appends rows, never rewrites existing ones

verbs.name: modify_doc_text
verbs.note: edits document text in place, ungated; Docs version history is the undo

verbs.name: create_doc
verbs.note: creates a new private Doc in the operator's Drive, ungated; reversible (trash)

verbs.name: create_spreadsheet
verbs.note: creates a new private Sheet, ungated; reversible (trash)

verbs.name: create_presentation
verbs.note: creates a new private Slides deck, ungated; reversible (trash)

verbs.name: create_form
verbs.note: creates a new Form, ungated; reversible (trash)

verbs.name: create_drive_file
verbs.note: creates a file in Drive (optionally from a URL — that URL is fetched server-side, an egress), ungated; reversible (trash)

verbs.name: create_drive_folder
verbs.note: creates a folder, ungated; reversible

verbs.name: import_to_google_doc
verbs.note: uploads local content as a new Doc, ungated; reversible

verbs.name: import_to_google_sheets
verbs.note: uploads local content as a new Sheet, ungated; reversible

verbs.name: import_to_google_slides
verbs.note: uploads local content as a new deck, ungated; reversible

verbs.name: send_message
verbs.note: posts to a Google Chat space as the operator, ungated; other people read it — preview, yes, send once

verbs.name: create_reaction
verbs.note: emoji reaction in Google Chat, ungated; reversible in the UI

verbs.name: create_script_project
verbs.note: creates an Apps Script project, ungated; reversible (delete in the editor)

verbs.name: update_script_content
verbs.note: FULL REPLACE of the project's files — any file absent from `files` is deleted with no undo; always get_script_content first and send back every file (appsscript JSON and every SERVER_JS). The most destructive tool at this tier

verbs.name: run_script_function
verbs.note: executes server-side code with whatever scopes the script holds, ungated; answers 403 cross-project unless the script's Cloud project is the OAuth client's — run scripts from the editor instead (CLAUDE.md)

verbs.name: modify_gmail_message_labels
verbs.note: extended tier; not loaded at core. Label/archive/trash mutations go through the Apps Script pipeline a human runs (CLAUDE.md)

verbs.name: batch_modify_gmail_message_labels
verbs.note: complete tier; not loaded at core

verbs.name: manage_gmail_label
verbs.note: extended tier; not loaded at core

verbs.name: manage_gmail_filter
verbs.note: extended tier; not loaded at core — a filter acts on every future message

verbs.name: delete_script_project
verbs.note: extended tier; not loaded at core

verbs.name: manage_drive_access
verbs.note: extended tier; not loaded at core — sharing changes are a human's in the Drive UI

verbs.name: set_drive_file_permissions
verbs.note: extended tier; not loaded at core

verbs.name: start_google_auth
verbs.note: complete tier; the consent flow starts itself from any read at core

risk.worst_case: mail sent, a calendar event deleted with invitees notified, a sheet range overwritten, or an Apps Script project's files erased by a full-replace update — all under the operator's own Google identity with no belt gate; the belt contributes registration, the tier list and the contract, and the core tier carries no Gmail label/trash tool, so inbox state cannot be destroyed from a session

mcp.note: The ${VAR} references are expanded by the MCP client from the environment it was launched in (Claude Code's documented ${VAR} expansion for mcpServers env); the belt never renders a literal secret into ~/.claude.json. Load the pair before launching the client: export GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID="$(security find-generic-password -s google-workspace-oauth | sed -n 's/.*"acct"<blob>="\(.*\)"/\1/p')" GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET="$(security find-generic-password -s google-workspace-oauth -w)". Codex reads the same two variables from ~/.codex/config.toml's [mcp_servers.google-workspace.env] — use "${VAR}" there too, or an env_keys passthrough where the harness supports one
